subject: HarborTech connector: 502 spikes and SLA escalation
messages:
From: HarborTech Support <support@harbortech.com>
To: sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>; marissa cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightPath Consulting <ops@brightpath.io>
Date: 2025-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Harbor connector 502 spikes in production

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

We're seeing recurring 502 spikes from the Redwood Harbor connector in our us-west deployment since ~08:45 PDT this morning. Traffic routing shows elevated retry rates and downstream timeouts for the features gating our payment reconciliation flow. Impact: intermittent failures for ~12% of requests, user-facing retries.

Attached are the aggregator logs and a short trace we pulled (harbor_logs_20250914.zip).

Can you confirm priority and next steps? Our SRE, BrightPath, is copied. We'd like an ETA for mitigation or a temporary workaround.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Technical Program Manager, HarborTech
lena.park@harbortech.com

Attachment: harbor_logs_20250914.zip (log bundle, 4.2MB)

From: sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@harbortech.com>
Cc: marissa cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vivek kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, BrightPath Consulting <ops@brightpath.io>
Date: 2025-09-14T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harbor connector 502 spikes in production

Thanks for the heads up, Lena — and sorry you're seeing this. I’m escalating to our partner ops and engineering liaisons. Quick notes:

- Priority set to P1 for partner connectors to HarborTech; we’ll aim for an initial response within 1 hour.
- Marissa (partner ops) will lead coordination on the SLA addendum and fastest mitigation path.
- Vivek will triage root-cause with logs you attached and our runtime team.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Try an explicit connection-failback rule on your side to route critical flows to the secondary region (if possible) — helps blunt user impact.
2) We’ll open an SUP ticket and share findings + temporary routing config within the hour.

Sharing SUP link when created. I’ll also schedule a 1-hr incident call at top of the hour.

Sergio Alvarez
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

---
(Internal note to Marissa/Vivek: please prioritize log analysis and confirm whether this looks like runtime kernel OOM vs. upstream routing. cc: platform-oncall)

From: marissa cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: sergio alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>; Lena Park <lena.park@harbortech.com>
Cc: vivek kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, BrightPath Consulting <ops@brightpath.io>
Date: 2025-09-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harbor connector 502 spikes in production

Lena — thanks, we reviewed the logs. Short summary and ask:

Summary of findings so far:
- Error pattern shows short-lived 502s correlated with a rolling kernel updates and batch window in Redwood Dedicated nodes serving HarborTech. No evidence of long-tail request serialization from your side.
- Root cause appears to be transient KV cache invalidation during a specific batch path; engineering is validating a fix.

Immediate plan (next 6 hours):
- Vivek will push a hotfix to the connector process to skip the problematic batch path (temporary mitigation).
- We’ll enable a conservative connection timeout and reduce batch aggregation for HarborTech routes to reduce retries.
- We propose an SLA addendum to cover 4-hr response for P1 partner incidents for the initial 30-day stabilization window while we roll the fix. Draft attached: SLA_addendum_draft_v1.pdf

Can HarborTech confirm acceptance of temporary addendum so we can apply the policy and commit operational hours? If accepted, we will:
- Mark the SUP ticket P1, target mitigation deploy in 3 hours, and provide hourly updates.

Thanks — will update within the hour with deploy ETA.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

---
Attachment: SLA_addendum_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Lena Park <lena.park@harbortech.com>

Cc: BrightPath Consulting <ops@brightpath.io>
Date: 2025-09-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harbor connector 502 spikes in production

Marissa — thanks for the quick analysis and the draft. We agree to a temporary 4-hr P1 response SLA for the 30-day stabilization window so your team can roll the hotfix. A few asks from HarborTech:

- Can Redwood commit to a daily status email (end-of-day) for the next 5 business days until we are stable?
- BrightPath will forward a small subset of expanded traces this afternoon to help root cause verification.
- We need the SUP ticket number and a signed copy of the addendum; we can circulate internally once received.

We’ve attached a short trace bundle as requested. Expect follow-up from our SRE.

Lena
